value.title: Drawer surface
value.summary: Five tasks, deliberately send-free: prompt list, drawer component, header wiring, capture-phase Escape, tests.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Phase 1 of the terminal prompt drawer. No delivery mechanics — the row actions call an injected callback so phase 2 swaps in the real sender without touching this component. This is the increment Jordan can exercise under HMR.

value.title: Prompt source module, git-tracked and held by a parity test
value.success: A typed prompt list ships in the feature directory, and a test fails when it diverges from Jordan's list file — and that test is honest on a clean CI checkout.
value.notes: SUPERSEDED by dce6ac368 (2026-08-09): the prompt list collapsed to a single authoring surface, PROMPT_TEXTS in lib/terminal-prompts.ts. lib/prompt-drawer-list.md was DELETED along with parsePromptList and the parity suite; with one copy there is nothing to keep in parity. ORIGINAL: The list lives at apps/web/src/features/064-terminal/lib/prompt-drawer-list.md — git-tracked, beside the parser. Resolve it from the repo root the way sibling tests do, and FAIL LOUDLY when absent rather than skipping.
value.note: Unblocked. Module, type, truncation and parser already ship and are unit-tested; only the file-reading parity test remains.
value.receipt: Mutation-verified twice — by the coder (3 mutations: text divergence, file moved, path repointed at gitignored scratch/) and independently re-run by me: moving the list away gave 2 failed / 24 passed with 0 SKIPPED, proving absence fails rather than skips. Restored byte-identical, suite back to 234/234 green.

value.title: TerminalPromptDrawer — panel geometry, truncated rows, two actions per row
value.success: The drawer renders one row per prompt showing its opening text plus an ellipsis with the full text on the row title, and each row carries a type action and a submit action.
value.notes: SEND-FREE BY DESIGN. Both actions call an injected callback prop — onSend(text, {submit}) — which phase 1 fills with a stub. Phase 2 swaps in the real sender without touching this component. Geometry: full height of the terminal body, about a third of the pane width, laid OVER the terminal rather than resizing it. Disable both actions when the connection is not live: use-terminal-socket.ts:199-203 makes a send a silent no-op on a closed socket, and the header already renders a ConnectionStatusBadge because it drops.

value.title: Wire the toggle into TerminalPaneHeader and give both hosts a positioning context
value.success: The toggle sits beside the theme picker, copy-buffer and close controls, and the drawer anchors correctly inside both the floating overlay and the inline split pane.
value.notes: TerminalPaneHeader is the single source of truth for shared controls (FX014, Plan 084) — put the button there and both surfaces gain it in one edit. terminal-overlay-panel.tsx roots at a fixed div and is already a containing block; terminal-split-pane.tsx:28 roots at a plain flex column and needs relative, or the drawer escapes and anchors to the viewport. Do not add a second control to either host — that re-creates the exact drift this component exists to end.

value.title: Capture-phase Escape ownership so the drawer does not close the terminal
value.success: With the drawer open, Escape closes the drawer and leaves the terminal open — including when focus is on the terminal or on the header toggle. With the drawer closed, Escape still closes the terminal as it does today.
value.notes: A React stopPropagation CANNOT work here and the cold validator proved why: terminal-overlay-panel.tsx:71-88 binds a document-level keydown in the BUBBLE phase, and the toggle is a SIBLING of the drawer in TerminalPaneHeader — so the event never passes through the drawer subtree. xterm's attachCustomKeyEventHandler (terminal-inner.tsx:225-238) returns true for bare Escape, so the terminal does not shield it either. Own a CAPTURE-phase document keydown while the drawer is open. Do NOT remove the existing binding — both hosts depend on it.

value.title: Phase 1 tests — truncation, both surfaces, Escape precedence, singleton stability
value.success: pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/ is green and covers the toggle on both hosts, row truncation, Escape with focus outside the drawer, and that opening the drawer does not remount the singleton.
value.notes: Write the Escape test with focus on the TERMINAL and on the TOGGLE. A test that fires Escape on a drawer node passes while the feature is broken — a green that lies, and the exact one the validator caught. Stub the injected onSend at the component boundary. Never mock the websocket, the pty, or tmux, and never tap a live tmux pane.

value.title: Row body submits; type-only stays distinct
value.success: Clicking anywhere on the row that is not an icon submits the prompt; the type icon still types without submitting and does not double-fire.
value.notes: The label is currently an inert span (terminal-prompt-drawer.tsx:111-117). Make the row body the primary submit action with a real interactive element and keyboard parity (Enter/Space), not a click handler on the li. Icon buttons must stopPropagation or sit outside the row hit area, or the type icon will also submit. Keep the type-only affordance visibly distinct: the row now fires a command at a coding agent, so a mis-tap has consequences.
value.receipt: Mutation-verified BOTH WAYS by the coder, each restored and diff-confirmed byte-identical. (1) Row button swapped for a div with onClick: the CLICK test still passed and the KEYBOARD test failed — which proves dw-0803 is load-bearing rather than decorative, since a div would have shipped a click-only control that looked correct. (2) Type icon made to also submit: dw-0802 and the existing tk-0003 type test both failed. Structure over promise: the row body is a SIBLING of the icon buttons, not an ancestor, so the DOM makes non-bubbling structural rather than relying on a stopPropagation someone has to keep.

value.title: Visual design pass on the drawer
value.success: Jordan looks at it and it reads as considered rather than utilitarian.
value.notes: Jordan verbatim: looks good technically, could probably dress it up a bit with a bit of front end design, doesnt need to look like 90s office software. Use the frontend-design skill. Stay inside the existing token system already in use here (bg-background, accent, muted-foreground, border) — do NOT introduce a parallel palette. Concrete starting points: text-xs with py-1.5 gives a very small target for what is now the primary action; 3.5 icon buttons carry no affordance until hover; the row reads as a table row rather than something you pick. Human-judgement acceptance (bp-0019) — no test can score this, so do not write one.

tk-0003.assertion: A row label renders truncated with an ellipsis and carries the full prompt text on its title.
Both row actions are disabled when the terminal connection is not live.
The drawer reads as full height and roughly a third of the pane width, over the terminal rather than resizing it.
tk-0003.note: Human-judgement by design (bp-0003, tier human-judgement). Holds until Jordan exercises the drawer under HMR — jsdom reports no computed layout, so a class assertion would prove the class was written, not that the proportion reads right.
tk-0003.receipt: Human verdict, Jordan 2026-08-08, verbatim: 'drawer looks good technically. coul dproably dress it up a bit though with a bit of front end design! doesnt need to look like 90s office software'. Geometry APPROVED — full height, ~1/3 width, overlaid not resizing. Visual polish is a separate, newly-raised concern tracked as ac-0015/tk-0008, not a defect in this assertion.

tk-0004.assertion: The toggle renders in the pane header on both the floating overlay and the inline split pane.
The drawer anchors inside the split pane, not to the viewport.
Opening the drawer neither remounts TerminalInner nor reconnects the websocket.

tk-0005.assertion: Escape with the drawer open and focus on the TERMINAL closes the drawer and leaves the terminal open.
Escape with the drawer open and focus on the header TOGGLE behaves the same way.
Escape with the drawer closed still closes the terminal.

tk-0007.assertion: The whole terminal-feature suite is green.
Lint, format and typecheck are clean on the new files.

tk-0008.assertion: Clicking the row body calls the send callback with submit true.
Clicking the type icon calls it with submit false and does not also fire the row handler.
The row body is keyboard-operable — Enter or Space submits, and it is focusable.

tk-0009.assertion: Jordan judges the drawer visually acceptable under HMR.
tk-0009.receipt: Human verdict, Jordan 2026-08-09, verbatim: 'looks fine, please get the feature completed'. Design pass accepted; the Enter icon stays — argued as the SIGNIFIER that the row is armed rather than a duplicate control, since without it nothing on screen tells you clicking a line fires a command at an agent.

tk-0009.assertion: No new colour or spacing primitives outside the existing token system.
tk-0009.receipt: Design pass used only existing tokens — bg-popover, text-popover-foreground, muted-foreground, accent, ring, muted, border, and the app's own --radius scale. No new colour or spacing primitives; the palette is deliberately zero-chroma because the terminal behind it owns the colour.
